event: A friend my age recently bought a house.
rawInterpretation: I am falling behind in life.
alternateRealityChecks: People reach life milestones at different times.
Financial situations, opportunities, and priorities vary significantly.
One achievement does not represent a person's entire life.
Comparing your timeline to someone else's may not be meaningful.
revisedInterpretation: My life is following a different path, not necessarily a worse one.
chosenBehaviour: Focus on my own goals and progress.
outcomeOneWeekLater: I identified financial goals that are meaningful to me.

event: I made a mistake during a meeting.
alternateRealityChecks: Everyone makes mistakes occasionally.
One mistake does not define your overall capability.
Competent people are not error-free.
Performance should be evaluated using broader evidence.
revisedInterpretation: I made a mistake, but that does not determine my competence.
chosenBehaviour: Correct the mistake and move on.
outcomeOneWeekLater: The issue was quickly forgotten and work continued normally.

event: I received positive feedback from several people but one person was critical.
rawInterpretation: The criticism proves I am not doing well.
alternateRealityChecks: You received both positive and constructive feedback.
Focusing only on criticism can create an incomplete picture.
Improvement opportunities and strengths can coexist.
The complete feedback should be considered.
revisedInterpretation: The criticism identifies an area to improve, but it does not invalidate the positive feedback.
chosenBehaviour: Learn from the feedback while acknowledging successes.
outcomeOneWeekLater: I felt more balanced about the situation.

event: I struggled to learn a new skill.
alternateRealityChecks: Learning often involves periods of confusion and difficulty.
Skill acquisition takes time and practice.
Difficulty does not indicate lack of intelligence.
The challenge may reflect the complexity of the skill.
revisedInterpretation: I am still learning, and difficulty is part of the process.

event: I was rejected after interviewing for a role.
rawInterpretation: Nobody will ever hire me for the type of work I want.
alternateRealityChecks: One rejection cannot predict all future outcomes.
Hiring decisions depend on many factors.
Being interviewed suggests there was initial interest.
Future opportunities remain possible.
revisedInterpretation: The rejection is disappointing but does not define my future prospects.
chosenBehaviour: Continue applying and improving my interview skills.

event: I saw people on social media sharing impressive achievements.
rawInterpretation: Everyone is more successful than me.
alternateRealityChecks: People typically share highlights rather than struggles.
Social media is not a complete representation of reality.
Success has different meanings for different people.
You may not be seeing the full context.
revisedInterpretation: I am comparing my full life to other people's highlights.
chosenBehaviour: Reduce comparison and focus on personal goals.
outcomeOneWeekLater: I felt less influenced by social media.

alternateRealityChecks: Reasonable people can disagree.
Disagreement does not prove that one side is foolish.
Different experiences often lead to different viewpoints.
Ideas can be debated without judging intelligence.
revisedInterpretation: The disagreement reflects different perspectives, not my worth.

alternateRealityChecks: People occasionally forget things.
One oversight does not define overall reliability.
Reliability should be evaluated across many situations.
Systems and reminders can prevent future mistakes.
revisedInterpretation: I made a mistake and can improve how I organise tasks.

event: I received a compliment but felt uncomfortable accepting it.
rawInterpretation: They are probably just being polite.
alternateRealityChecks: The compliment may genuinely reflect their perception.
People often offer praise because they mean it.
Rejecting positive feedback can create a distorted self-image.
There is no evidence that the compliment was insincere.
revisedInterpretation: The compliment may reflect something I genuinely did well.
outcomeOneWeekLater: I found it easier to acknowledge strengths.

event: I am slower than some colleagues at completing tasks.
rawInterpretation: I am less capable than they are.
alternateRealityChecks: Speed is only one aspect of contribution.
Different people prioritise quality, depth, and accuracy differently.
Experience and context vary significantly.
Capability cannot be measured by speed alone.
revisedInterpretation: My value depends on more than how quickly I complete tasks.
chosenBehaviour: Focus on quality and continuous improvement.
outcomeOneWeekLater: My work quality was positively recognised.

event: I often avoid sharing ideas because I assume they are not good enough.
rawInterpretation: Other people always have better ideas than I do.
alternateRealityChecks: You cannot know how others will evaluate an idea before sharing it.
Many useful ideas initially seem imperfect.
Ideas improve through discussion and feedback.
Remaining silent guarantees that potentially good ideas are not heard.
revisedInterpretation: I cannot accurately judge how others will respond without sharing my ideas.

event: My performance review rated me as meeting expectations instead of exceeding them.
alternateRealityChecks: Meeting expectations often indicates solid performance.
A rating reflects performance during a period, not personal worth.
Performance exists on a spectrum rather than fixed categories.
One evaluation does not define identity.
revisedInterpretation: The review provides feedback on performance, not my value as a person.
chosenBehaviour: Use the review to identify growth opportunities.
outcomeOneWeekLater: I gained more clarity on development goals.

event: I feel behind because I have not achieved a goal I expected by this age.
alternateRealityChecks: Life goals rarely follow a fixed timeline.
Past experiences often contribute valuable skills and insights.
Many successful outcomes occur later than originally planned.
A delayed goal does not mean failure.
revisedInterpretation: My timeline differs from my expectations, but my experiences still have value.
chosenBehaviour: Refocus on future steps instead of past comparisons.
outcomeOneWeekLater: I felt more motivated about future plans.

event: I rarely notice my achievements because I immediately focus on the next challenge.
rawInterpretation: Nothing I achieve is ever enough.
alternateRealityChecks: Progress deserves recognition even when new goals exist.
Achievement and growth can coexist.
Ignoring accomplishments creates an incomplete picture of reality.
Acknowledging success does not mean becoming complacent.
revisedInterpretation: I can appreciate achievements while still pursuing improvement.
outcomeOneWeekLater: I felt more balanced about my development.

event: Several people have recently given feedback that I tend to underestimate my contributions.
rawInterpretation: They are just trying to make me feel better.
alternateRealityChecks: Consistent feedback from multiple people may contain useful information.
Others sometimes notice strengths that we overlook.
It is possible to have strengths without being perfect.
The feedback may be worth exploring rather than dismissing.
revisedInterpretation: There may be aspects of my contribution that I am not fully recognising.
chosenBehaviour: Track achievements and seek objective feedback.
outcomeOneWeekLater: I identified several contributions that I had previously minimised.
